text: When a documentation AC fixes a COUNT of drawn elements (end points, branches, labels), that count is a drift vector: it is stated in criteria, restated in a test_spec descriptor NAME, and restated again in notes and it_requirements. Decide the count by asking which STEPS the diagram already draws and enumerating every terminal disposition of those steps -- not by counting the sibling records the criteria happen to cite. A step drawn with a single outcome asserts that the step cannot fail. Corollary for staleness descriptors: a liveness check (every referenced id still resolves) can never catch a sibling ADDED later; only the completeness direction (every behavioural leaf under the parent is referenced) does, and the usual reason for withholding completeness -- red on arrival -- disappears the moment the omission it would have flagged is fixed. Discriminate behavioural leaves from documentation leaves by change_target (pipeline vs docs).

INF-1300 decomposition: when a pinned CLI contract cannot produce a committable artifact, the honest BA split is three-way, not two-way. Widen the inputs ONLY for facts the caller demonstrably already holds and the authoring surface already obliges them to hold (here: the parent doc and the source ticket); refuse for facts that are diagram CONTENT (the per-genre related_code/related_surfaces/related_agents); and never emit a placeholder, because check_doc_frontmatter BLOCKS on a path-valued field whose paths do not exist, so the most helpful-looking implementation inverts the acceptance promise. Two measured store facts worth reusing: (1) config/diagram_types.json declares requires_frontmatter per genre but NO commit-time check enforces presence -- diagram_type_validators only validates the NAME -- so a check-set-only observation reports a green that says nothing about the obligation; (2) check_mermaid_parent_link needs THREE things (parent: frontmatter, prose Parent: line, reciprocal children:), not the two SKILL.md 6a describes, and it fires on any doc containing a mermaid fence, i.e. every scaffolded doc. Also: SKILL.md section 4 attributes the Legend to ADR-015, which is about noqa BLE001 suppression; the six docs carrying a Legend show three different shapes (C4 element key, flowchart shape key, per-diagram edge-trust tables), so a fixed verbatim legend is not merely unsourced, it is the wrong requirement -- derive the key per genre from the declared vocabulary and mark the authored part.

On a ticket where files_touched are documentation/config surfaces tightly coupled to a code fix (GE-127d-1: reconciling a stale published rule with the enforced one), python-coder may correct the prose/comment surfaces directly as part of the same diff rather than leaving them for documentation-expert to author. In that shape, documentation-expert's phase is a verification pass -- grep every stale-claim wording for remaining occurrences, confirm the doc genre (reference vs how-to etc.) still matches the AC's documentation_triggers, and check the 'related'/'context' cross-linked docs for the same stale claim -- rather than a new-authoring dispatch to a specialist writer. Don't assume files_touched naming documentation-expert means prose is still unwritten; read the diff first.

Enriching documentation ACs: the surface decision the BA delegates to the it-po is usually settled by a MECHANICAL constraint rather than an editorial one. check-doc-length ratchets against a 300-line limit -- a file already over it may not GROW, while shrinking or holding steady passes -- and it is pre-commit-only, so it runs in no CI job and a violation appears only as a local refusal. In leafcutter today docs/testing/README.md is 326 lines and the root CLAUDE.md is 820, so: new material must go in a NEW file (a new file is not growth), any pointer added to an over-limit file must be offset by an equal removal in the same commit, and an edit to a standing rule in CLAUDE.md must be a REPLACEMENT that does not increase its line count. Second reusable pattern, for test contracts on prose: only clauses the BA deliberately wrote as absences or as copy-runnable steps are mechanically checkable -- test them by EXECUTING what the document says (extract the command/marker from the page and run it), never by asserting a string is present, since a guide naming a flag the runner rejects passes a presence check and teaches the reader that the suite is broken. State the remaining reader-outcome clauses as reader-trial verification in test_rationale rather than approximating them with a grep for the file. Third: when a criterion forbids a number, enumerate every possible enforcement point and name which one actually gates -- 'the page must not restate the recorded budget' is VACUOUS while the budget record is still empty, so the check that forbids any duration literal is the load-bearing one.

A review verdict reported back to the dispatching agent in prose is NOT the same as recording it on the ticket, and the gap is invisible until someone re-reads the ticket cold. On this ticket a round-3 pr-reviewer sign-off decision (resolve to ok, carry two medium hardening notes forward) was reached and relayed to the caller, but the ticket's own frontmatter, Sign-offs checklist, and Comments section still showed the round-1 'failed' state from two rounds earlier -- because reporting a verdict and writing it back via the signoff skill's atomic recipe are two different actions, and only the second one survives past the current session. Any phase agent (not just pr-reviewer) that reasons its way to a verdict mid-session must still perform the full signoff atomic write before the phase is considered complete; a verdict that exists only in a message to the caller is functionally lost the moment the session ends.

This gate's two scoping restraints (append-only edits; auto-fix evidence limited to files_touched intersect diff) are not just safety rails against overwriting good data -- their REFUSALS are diagnostic signal. On GE-127d-1 the gate correctly declined to drop a stale implemented_by ticket-path entry (append-only) and correctly declined to add the real implementation file check_file_size_rule_parity.py (files_touched was stale and omitted it), and reporting both refusals as findings rather than silently accepting the gap is what got files_touched corrected upstream. A gate whose auto-fix silently no-ops on a legitimate case, with no comment recording why, hides the exact defect (stale ticket metadata) that a downstream reader needs surfaced. Separately: a verdict reached and reported to a dispatching agent in one session is not durable until it is written to the ticket via the signoff atomic recipe in that same session -- this gate itself reconciled the AC store and returned ok without ever touching the ticket's frontmatter/Sign-offs/Comments, leaving 'needed' on disk for a week until a follow-up dispatch asked for the bookkeeping explicitly.

commit_guardian.json's hooks_manifest.hooks[] is itself a mechanically-enforced ADR contract (ADR-038 Amendment 2's change_set_source field, checked by change_set_source.py's determine_change_set_sources()). Any ticket whose Implementation Notes add or edit a manifest entry therefore trips has_adr_contract_change=true and is architecturally LARGE regardless of the file/component-count thresholds -- architect-review should check whether a change touches hooks_manifest.hooks[] before applying the small-case file-count rubric on commit_guardian tickets.

Touching a contract an ADR pins does not by itself mean the ADR should be amended. Amend when the contract itself changes; write a NEW ADR (citing the old one as adopted-not-modified) when the ticket merely COMPLIES with the existing contract and its real decisions are about something else -- write-adr.md section 1 says implementing an accepted ADR's contract needs a citation, not an amendment. GE-127d-1 declares change_set_source on a new hooks_manifest entry (ADR-038 Amendment 2 compliance) while its actual decisions are about published-vs-enforced reconciliation, so it became ADR-045 rather than ADR-038 Amendment 3. Also: check_adr_collision.py and adr_refs.py both resolve git state from cwd, so run them via env --chdir into the git root -- from a non-repo parent, check_adr_collision.py fails open-looking with a git diff --no-index usage dump and exit 1.

ADR number allocation: check_adr_collision.py derives its change set from the git INDEX, not argv, so running it with nothing staged exits 0 having examined zero files -- a vacuous pass that structurally cannot see a sibling branch's claim. It also lives at templates/scripts/commit_guardian/, not the scripts/commit_guardian/ path the adr-author template prescribes, so the template's prescribed invocation fails with ENOENT. Concretely, on BO-400e-1 the architect suggested ADR-045 and it was ALREADY claimed by two remote in-flight branches (observed-refusal-establishes-protection and published-rule-reconciliation-gate) while the guard stayed silent. Reliable procedure: scripts/adr_refs.py 'Unclaimed numbers' (no file AND no citation) plus a grep for ADR-0NN across refs/remotes -- never ls | tail -1, never a ticket-comment suggestion unre-verified, and never the guard alone. adr_refs.py takes ~2 min on this repo, so start it early and do other reading while it runs.

knowledge-management AC authoring, 2026-09-30: a NEW tree here should use a plain KM-NNN id (KM-400), not a new compound sub-prefix -- derive_parent_id mis-derives KM-XXX-400a to 'KM-XXX', which silently breaks the parent/child hooks. The inverse is the useful half: on a plain-prefix KM tree the hooks DO fire, so the parent's covered_by and each child's depends_on are load-bearing rather than conventional, unlike the KM-ADM-* and KM-KGS-* families. Also: the PROJECT_CONTEXT warning 'pass FILES, never a directory' to validate_ac_schema.py is now STALE -- KI-ACS-001 was fixed 2026-08-19, a directory is walked recursively and a zero-file run exits non-zero; verified directly (OK: all 8 AC YAML files are valid). Four standing boundaries for any new KM capability: KM-KGS-100 owns the map's content vs a contract over it; KM-ADM-100b owns ABSENT relations while a CONTRADICTION between two asserting sources is a different answer; ACS-1100 is inherited via a doc_links relationship:context entry and never copied; and reporting that work is built-but-unproved (a read) must never be confused with writing a done badge (a write, owned by phase_store_record_health/TQ-400).

INF-600a-1 (L2, reviewed, todo) is the record that created the two rival agent-registry skill fields: it makes skills_invoked authoritative and keeps skills_used as an alias. Any AC work that moves the skill list into agent-template frontmatter directly contradicts it and must amend or supersede it explicitly. Also: INF-600 sits at its 12-child cap under a standing waiver, so new L1s about agent self-description cannot go there; and template_compiler.py holds two rival per-agent injection designs side by side - a placeholder-gated one that reached 0 of 60 agents and a frontmatter-flag-gated one (signoff) that reached 23 of 23. Prefer the flag design when specifying any per-agent injection.

Authoring L2/L3 under TQ-600a (2026-10-05). THE TRAP THAT COST A VALIDATION ROUND, and it is not in any doc: declares_side_effect is derived by check_ac_schema, and the derivation window is opened by _THEN_CLAUSE_START_RE = re.compile(r'\bThen\b', re.IGNORECASE) -- CASE-INSENSITIVE. So a mid-sentence lowercase 'then' anywhere in your GIVEN opens the window early, and every durable-effect phrase after it counts, contrary to the reference doc's statement that a Given is excluded. Second half of the same trap: _DURABLE_EFFECT_RE contains the bare alternative 'deployed to' with NO trailing word boundary, so the ordinary phrase 'the deployed tooling' MATCHES it. Combined, 'and then asserts on what the deployed tooling does' in a Given derives declares_side_effect: true and blocks the commit on an AC with no durable effect at all. Fix is to reword, not to author the flag -- authoring true would force user-surface-smoker into the generated ticket for an internal pipeline AC. Check your Givens for lowercase 'then' before trusting a clean schema run. SECOND REUSABLE FACT: the hook seams differ per hook and getting them wrong gives a silent false pass. check_ac_schema reads HOOK_TEST_STAGED_FILES; check_ac_limits and check_ac_parent_covered_by read HOOK_TEST_FILES; all three resolve the store from cwd unless HOOK_ROOT is set, and from a non-repo cwd they fail OPEN with exit 0 and no output. check_ac_parent_covered_by additionally needs PYTHONPATH=<worktree root> so 'scripts.ac_store.ac_parent_id' imports -- its strategy 2 (script-relative) fails when you run the templates/ copy, and it prints 'RESULT: could_not_check' which is NOT a pass. Verify a gate produced its OVERRIDE ACTIVE / finding line before believing it ran. THIRD: scan_ac_orphans.py parent-links --ac-root <abs path> is the independent check on parent covered_by and works from any cwd; use it to corroborate. STORE-WIDE BASELINE at origin/main 3ec14b85: 47 pre-existing parent-link orphans across ACS-300g-1, BO-100d, BP-100b, FIN-100, INF-100c, KM-200, KM-KGS-100e, TKT-100 and seven UXP trees -- expect that output and do not read it as damage you caused. FOURTH, specification-level: when an existing L1's notes state a BINARY boundary ('read versus mutate') and new measurement finds three cases, amend the parent's notes in the same batch as the new children. The old note actively misdirects the next BA, and the amended_by entry alone does not reach anyone reading notes. Here 'mutate' turned out to be alter-the-package-before-the-deploy (keeps a real deploy; the failing deploy IS the test) versus alter-the-result-after-it (needs a copy, 91x cheaper), which is a route, not a refinement.

Authoring TQ-600a-11/-12 (2026-10-05). TWO declared_files SCHEMA TRAPS NOT IN docs/reference/ac-schema.md, both caught by validate_ac_schema.py on the first run: (1) declared_files[].state accepts ONLY 'existing' or 'to_be_created' -- the intuitive 'new' is rejected; (2) a declared path must be in canonical form, so a directory written with a trailing slash ('unit_tests/ac_store/') is rejected. For a test file that does not exist yet, write the concrete file path with state: to_be_created, not the directory. THIRD TRAP, pure YAML and easy to miss in a long doc_links block: an unquoted doc_links[].relevance whose value contains a colon ('ELIGIBLE. Subject: which root a marker routes to.') is a YAML parse error at that line, because the second colon is read as a mapping separator. Every other relevance in the same file used the '>-' folded form and was fine. Use '>-' uniformly rather than inline scalars. FOURTH, specification-level and reusable: when a measured lever does not match any existing L1's stated MECHANISM, say so in the record rather than restating the lever to fit. TQ-600a's criteria name SHARING ('produced once and shared'); the libyaml-parser lever makes the work cheap instead, and a parse cannot be shared across OS processes. Filed it under TQ-600a anyway for delivery speed, but recorded the mismatch in the child's notes AND in the parent's amended_by with the exact re-parenting recipe (two fields: child depends_on, both parents' covered_by). A BA cannot author an L1, so naming the misfit precisely is the only honest move available -- silently stretching the parent's criteria is how an AC tree stops meaning anything. FIFTH, concurrency: when a sibling branch has already raised a parent's child_limit_override and authored children not yet on main, pick an override value that is correct AFTER both merge (here 12, not the 10 the other branch sets), and state in the amended_by that the conflict resolution is 12 rather than either side -- otherwise the merge resolver takes one side and the cap is wrong by two.

TQ-600a-9/-10/-13 authoring. FIRST, and it cost nothing to check: a parent's amended_by can RESERVE ids in prose that were never used. TQ-600a's 8->12 override said TQ-600a-9 and -10 'were authored on a separate branch and are not yet reachable from main'. Two commands disproved it -- `git log --all --diff-filter=A -- '**/TQ-600a-9*.yaml' '**/TQ-600a-10*.yaml'` returns nothing, and `git log --all -S 'TQ-600a-9' -- docs/acceptance-criteria/` returns only the override that reserved them. Never trust a prose id reservation; it is a claim about the store, and the store is checkable. Correct the stale premise in the new amended_by entry rather than silently working around it. SECOND, the shape that makes a speed AC safe: when the change is 'share one expensive artifact across N tests that differ only in assertions', the build-count criterion is NOT the load-bearing one -- the discrimination criterion is. Break each member's own subject in turn and require exactly that member to go red. Without it, sharing is satisfiable by a change that makes N-1 assertions true by construction, and the suite gets faster and weaker at once with every test still green. THIRD, when the evidence marks an item MEDIUM / 'not instrumented', the criterion must require the measurement AND pre-agree the response to a null result ('revert rather than keep on the strength of the file-count argument'). A persuasive structural argument will otherwise survive a contrary measurement; deciding the revert after the change is written is a decision nobody makes well. FOURTH, timing criteria on this shared WSL host must be ratios measured in one sitting, never absolute second thresholds -- an absolute threshold is flaky, fails on a loaded day, and gets deleted. FIFTH, when a proposal revises a decision a previous author WROTE DOWN in the source (here: 'install_1 is never shared or reused so no test is order-dependent'), file it as its own separate child, not as a clause of the uncontested work, so it can be refused on its own without blocking the rest -- and make the discharge behavioural (run the group forwards, reversed, and each member alone; same verdicts) rather than argumentative. SIXTH, a documented protection with zero enforcement is authorable as a behavioural AC without becoming a grep test: assert that a REAL default collection and the documented exclusion AGREE, read the document only to learn what claim is being made, and require the comparison be shown to fail on an introduced disagreement. This is the fourth instance in this repo of 'a check that examined nothing looked like a check that found nothing'. SEVENTH, hook verification trap hit live: check_ac_schema.py and check_ac_parent_covered_by.py both exited 0 from the workspace parent having read '0 staged files'; only check_ac_parent_covered_by printed 'RESULT: could_not_check'. Run them with `env -C <worktree-root>` and prefer a hook that NAMES what it inspected -- check_ac_limits printed 'parent TQ-600a has 13 L2 children', which is the only output in the set that proves the staged parent was actually read.

Amending TQ-600a-11 after its wholesale YAML-loader migration was narrowed from ~113 call sites to one. FIRST, the reusable AC shape: an adoption criterion written as 'EVERY entry point must use X, except a documented allowlist' puts the maintained list on the side that grows (here ~81 source files and rising) and makes the seam test rot by default. Invert it -- 'nothing may use X except this small DECLARED set' -- and the maintained list is bounded, the test fails in the direction that actually caused harm (silent re-spread of a permissive parser into guardrail paths), and it needs a non-empty assertion so deleting the last adopter is a failure rather than a vacuous pass. SECOND, the admission test for a faster-but-not-identical dependency must be four-part and conjunctive: measured volume at THAT call site; no dependence on a RAISED error; no equivalence contract with the reference implementation; not a BLOCK/PASS decision point. The defect class is silent -- the fast arm returns a VALUE where the slow arm raised, so a fail-open `except` turns 'skip this malformed file' into 'accept it' with nothing in the logs. THIRD, write the criterion about VOLUME, not about files: in generate_agent_cards.py the whole-store walk kept the fast parser and the sibling per-template frontmatter parse was reverted, so the same file earns opposite verdicts at different volumes. FOURTH, a repointed speed claim needs three companion assertions or it is gameable: identical output between arms, equal and non-zero parsed counts, and both raw arm figures printed, so 'the host was loaded' and 'the code left the fast path' are distinguishable. Ratio against a same-sitting baseline only -- this host shows 3.8x-10.74x variation with zero code change, and this record's FIRST amendment was already caused by reasoning from absolute figures taken in another sitting. FIFTH, before trusting 'N call sites survive', grep for production callers: one of TQ-600a-11's two surviving sites (_scan_ac_assignments) has no caller outside its own tests, so the live surface was one, and a timing test pointed at it would have measured dead code. SIXTH, a retraction that lives only in prose gets re-litigated -- pair it with a discrimination test that goes RED when someone re-applies the retracted change (feed the required gate an input only the permissive parser accepts). SEVENTH, store-hygiene finds that cost nothing: a doc_link stuck at status:planned whose file has since landed on main, a doc_link path pointing at a module that was later split, and a cross-record citation (TQ-600a-9 citing '3.8x to 10.74x recorded in TQ-600a-11') for a figure that was never actually in the cited record.

Enriching TQ-600a-13-ii..xi (nightly run of _MANUAL tests + per-PR 'Nightly suite status' hold). FIRST, assignment: no registry agent owns GitHub Actions YAML; workflow-architect is a user-spawned non-phase supervisor, so workflow ACs go to python-coder -- and the assignment is made correct by architecture: all decision logic in a stdlib Python module under scripts/ci/ (package-internal, no templates counterpart, no deploy-manifest entry), the workflow a thin caller (precedent ci.yml consumer-install-sim). SECOND, the behavioural-not-grep rule for workflows is satisfiable cheaply with ONE shared harness: a stdlib HTTP recording fake of the GitHub API on 127.0.0.1 used through the REAL REST client (so error mapping/pagination are exercised), plus a workflow-step executor that locates a job by exact name and runs its run: steps verbatim, skipping only uses: steps and an exact-match prep list, and FAILING on any ${{ }} in a run step (which doubles as the script-injection rule) or on a matrix. One seam per workflow file. THIRD, measured costs that make this affordable: a synthetic child pytest session costs 0.21s with PYTEST_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD=1 vs 1.39s without; a depth-1 clone of this repo costs 5.16s, so 'scratch clone of the repository' must be a synthetic git repo with a local bare origin. FOURTH, a measured trap: re-running failing node ids WITHOUT -m manual under addopts -m 'not manual' deselects them (exit 5, zero run) -- a retry that drops the opt-in turns every red night green. FIFTH, GitHub facts that reshape gate ACs: a skipped job reports as a PASSING required check (so a required check job must have no job-level if:); widening ci.yml's pull_request types for label/edit events would re-run every shard, so event-driven gates need their own workflow; GET /repos/{o}/{r}/rules/branches/main is readable without admin on a public repo, so 'is it required' can be read automatically even when it cannot be edited. SIXTH, sibling contradiction pattern: an L3 that bounds allowed writes (no issue-body edits) plus an L3 demanding 'exactly one read' plus an L3 whose comment needs the latest streak state -> state lives in comments and costs a second read; surface it as a PENDING USER DECISION rather than silently choosing.

IT PO enrichment in guardrail-engine: before pinning WHERE a fix lands, measure the target file against its own commit-time gate. scripts/adr_refs.py is 576 lines against a 400-line .py limit and templates/scripts/commit_guardian/check_doc_length.py is 359/400 (41 left), so both fixes must go into sibling/helper modules or the commit is refused by the same family of gate being edited; docs/pre-commit-hooks.md is 292/300, which decides a documentation-placement question mechanically rather than by taste. Second reusable rule: a module placed in templates/scripts/commit_guardian/ needs NO deploy-map line (build_commit_guardian in scripts/build_phases_lifecycle.py rglobs the whole directory) while a module anywhere else does -- so the deploy-manifest obligation is a question about WHICH directory, not about whether the module is new. Third: scripts/commit_guardian/_resolve_root.py is an UNTRACKED build output, so a tracked repo script must never import it; run git ls-files before declaring a shared helper reachable. Fourth: find_project_root() has 43 callers under templates/scripts/commit_guardian/ and cannot express failure at all (cwd git read, then a __file__ walk keyed on .git OR CLAUDE.md, then 'two levels up'), so a failable resolver must be ADDED alongside it rather than changing its contract.

Closing a required-check name spoof with a dedicated GitHub App (TQ-600a-13-vi/-x, 2026-10-09): pinning the ruleset context to the App's integration id is necessary but not sufficient. If the App's private key is a REPOSITORY Actions secret, any same-repository pull_request workflow a PR adds receives it (VERIFIED in TQ-600a-13-xvi's notes) and can mint the App's own token, so the spoof moves rather than closes; the credential must be an environment secret whose deployment-branch policy admits only main, and 'a PR-added workflow cannot read it' must be a recorded live observation before the ruleset change. Other non-obvious criteria for any App-published required check: create the check run in_progress BEFORE computing the verdict (a crash then leaves a non-green check instead of none); conclude only success or failure, never neutral or skipped, which satisfy a required check; post on the event payload's head SHA, never GITHUB_SHA (main's tip under pull_request_target); rename the computing Actions job so it does not share the required name; and state the residual that a pass already published on a head commit cannot be withdrawn by an evaluation that cannot mint the credential. Decomposition note: amending existing records (-vi check definition, -x ruleset pin) plus consequential siblings (-xi allowed-write list, which explicitly refused check-run creation; -xvii break-glass, which restored the context with the old source) beat adding a 20th child under an L2 that already has 19.

When a user decision names ONE instance of a defect class to remediate (e.g. 'remove architect-review-deep so the build goes green'), probe the whole class on the real data before writing the remediation as sufficient. The registry had two template-less spawn targets (architect-review-deep AND conflict-resolver-deep, both already counted in ADR-035), so a 'refuse on unresolvable sub-agent' gate stays red after the named fix. Write the remediation for the decided instance, state the measured residual as a blocker for a user decision, and keep any real-tree test from asserting zero findings until it is decided. Related agent-registry convention: when a second granted-thing (spawn allowlist) follows the first (skills), generalise the existing validators over (declaration-key, invoking-tool) or by field (derived-copy comparator, transform-hook scope, preparation registration) rather than adding sibling checks, and amend the approved first-slice records' scope constraints with amended_by so their pinning tests move with them.

Any 'durable location' AC built on the build-time declaration (config/knowledge_sink.json) must check how per-drive worktrees are provisioned, not just what the declaration says: setup_ticket_worktree.py runs build.py --target-dir <worktree>, so every drive's deployed declaration names the disposable worktree root (8 worktrees already hold their own knowledge_emissions.jsonl). The fix is for the bootstrap to inherit the main install's RECORDED root (read <main_repo>/.leafcutter/config/knowledge_sink.json), never to compute it from main_repo's path, which in the dev workspace is leafcutter-ai/ rather than the install root. Also verify declaration lookups against the DEPLOYED layout: emit_event.py searches <ancestor>/config/knowledge_sink.json, which never matches the real <project>/.leafcutter/config/ location, so INF-400c-4-iii shipped as done while the lookup was unreachable. Split pattern for log-sink work: build+bootstrap (python-coder) / writers (python-coder) / readers (python-coder) / prompt overrides (llm-expert) / docs, with documentation-gate records as L3s when the L1 is at its 5-L2 cap.

Placement in the GE-120/GE-126 family: Pattern A (horizontal L0 split) is MECHANICALLY INERT here and must not be proposed as a way to free an L1 slot under GE-120. check_ac_limits.py derives a parent from the id STRING, so moving GE-120g to a new L0 leaves it counted under GE-120; freeing a slot would require renaming an existing GE-120x plus every descendant, which breaks test module names, ticket references and ADR links. The working move, with three in-repo precedents inside three weeks (BP-1600 over a capped BP-100, BP-1300 before it, GE-125 over GE-123e), is a NEW ROOT L0 carrying the new L1 — no existing record is renamed and no child_limit_override is needed. A deliberately sparse L0 (one L1) is acceptable and precedented: BP-1600 shipped that way on 2026-09-07 and said so; the sparse advisory is non-blocking, and padding a tree to reach the three-child floor with L1s that belong to another owner is worse than sparseness. Also: GE-126's two free L1 slots have now been examined and rejected on SUBJECT three times (GE-120f, GE-128, GE-129) - stop re-litigating them; its reader is someone interrogating the guard system, and the liveness regime's records that already sit there are recorded as a capacity artifact to be undone, not a precedent to extend. Finally, ACS-800 is NOT a placement precedent (it is the unbuilt opaque-UID restructure); the only thing it supplies is the statement that child_limit_override is a temporary stopgap it exists to retire.

GE-129a decomposition: settings.json hook entries are JSON objects {type,command,timeout} with NO identifier - not bare command strings, so the binding question is about the editor parsers tolerance of unknown keys, not about the files shape. The durable BA move was to fix the binding PROPERTY (derived from event+matcher+resolved script at run time; a repointed entry leaves both the declaration tied to nothing and the entry undeclared) and leave the declarations location to the IT PO. Seam against BP-1600a-1 is sharper than stated: BP-1600a-1 already reads settings.json but reduces it to a SET OF SCRIPTS, so the same guard wired at two events is one wired script there and two subjects here - that sentence is what stops the two records reading as duplicates. Also: this surface is several surfaces - a guard wired after a tool call cannot stop it, so a declaration can be faultless and unusable at once.

GE-129 enrichment, three reusable findings. (1) ONE RUNNER vs TWO is decidable from the BA's own decomposition: when the seams a BA cuts are exactly enumerate / bind / present-and-read, they ARE a population-reader-plus-adapter interface, and a second runner duplicates every population-agnostic part (vocabulary, rollup, unresolved verdict, outcome propagation). Choosing one runner keeps an approved sibling's once-written clause reaching the new population WITHOUT amending it - but 'already covered' is an assertion until a failure-angle descriptor drives the new population to empty and asserts the SAME verdict path fires. Also state the figure PER POPULATION, or a shared runner silently changes the approved record's observable behaviour. (2) AN AGENT-ASSIGNMENT PRECEDENT MUST BE CHECKED FOR ITS DISCRIMINATOR, NOT ITS CONCLUSION: GE-120f-5 went documentation-expert -> llm-expert only because its surface included templates/skills/*/SKILL.md, which fires llm-expert's registry DSL literally. For a docs-only session-hook page that discriminator is absent (create-hook scaffolds PRE-COMMIT hooks and the how-to says the two systems are completely separate), so documentation-expert is correct. Applying the precedent's conclusion without its discriminator turns a precedent into a habit. (3) DO NOT SPLIT A DOCUMENTATION AC AT THE WRITE/EXECUTE SEAM when the executable half IS the anti-vacuity: the writing remainder collapses to 'the document states X', which is grep-checkable and disqualified. Carry the python obligation as a hard it_requirement plus descriptors instead - GE-120f-5's precedent. MEASUREMENT CORRECTION worth carrying: both natural homes for session-hook docs are over the 300-line doc-length ratchet - docs/reference/claude-code-hooks.md 334 AND docs/how-to/creating-a-claude-code-hook.md 378, the latter being the document the walkthrough clauses are actually about and the one prior notes never measured.

build_commit_guardian runs inject_config() over EVERY deployed .py file under templates/scripts/commit_guardian/, not just .json/.yaml/.md -- so a Python source file that contains the literal contiguous substring {{config.output_root}} (or any {{config.KEY}} placeholder) anywhere in its raw text, including inside its own string-literal constants and comments, gets that substring silently rewritten to the resolved value AT DEPLOY TIME. A runner that needs to recognise and substitute that token ITSELF at RUNTIME (e.g. to resolve a hook entry injected into the deployed manifest AFTER deploy time, which is exactly how out-of-process test fixtures are built) must therefore build its own token constant from non-contiguous concatenated string pieces (e.g. "{" + "{config.output_root}" + "}") so inject_config's regex cannot match it in the source text, while runtime string concatenation still yields the exact whole token. Symptom when this is missed: the substitution silently becomes a no-op, an unresolved token reaches subprocess.run() as a literal path segment, the child interpreter fails with its own generic 'can't open file' / 'No such file or directory' non-zero exit, and naive exit-code interpretation (nonzero = rejected) misreads that LAUNCH FAILURE as a genuine successful rejection -- two compounding bugs that both stayed invisible until a manual real-artifact spot-check outside the fixture-authored test suite (a hand-built second deployed copy with a hook injected directly into commit_guardian.json, mirroring the test module's own fixture technique) was run by hand.

A per-hook exit-code classifier layered on top of run_hook.py must not invent its own launch-failure taxonomy (a hard-coded substring blocklist over combined stdout+stderr) when run_hook.py ALREADY emits a structured, parseable not-run report for exactly this purpose: `RESULT: not_run checker=<target> reason=<reason>` via check_outcome.emit_not_run(), with distinct reason values (could_not_start exits 1, disabled exits 0) that a substring grep will silently under-cover -- check_negative_controls.py's _LAUNCH_FAILURE_MARKERS list catches could_not_start (coincidentally, because the reason string contains that substring) but has no entry for disabled, so a disabled hook's not-run report (exit 0) falls through to the 'genuinely ran and produced a clean result' branch. This is reachable via a real, already-existing pattern in commit_guardian.json: two hooks_manifest entries (check-ac-tree-limits, check-ticket-ac-limits) already share the same underlying script (check_ac_limits.py), and run_hook.py's _is_target_disabled() matches by SCRIPT BASENAME rather than by hook id -- so disabling either one of a same-script pair would make an invocation of the OTHER one's negative control observe the sibling's disablement instead of its own behaviour. General lesson for any future verifying-surface built on top of run_hook.py (ADR-045 section 7's family): derive state from the dispatcher's own structured outcome vocabulary (check_outcome.py), never re-derive a parallel one via output-text pattern matching -- and check hooks_manifest for basename collisions before trusting any per-hook-id classification that a name-keyed helper (like _is_target_disabled) might silently resolve against a different id.

Resolution-side note to pair with pr-reviewer's H-1 capture (line above): once a per-hook exit-code classifier correctly parses run_hook.py's structured not-run protocol, a second, independent misclassification risk remains on the OPPOSITE side and is easy to miss because it produces no not-run report at all -- a real argparse-based check that has not declared a positional argument will treat an appended known-bad-input token as an unrecognised CLI argument and let argparse's OWN ArgumentParser.error() reject it (a 'usage: ...' line, Python's hard-coded parser-error exit code 2) BEFORE the check's own examination logic ever runs. A bare 'non-zero exit = rejection observed' rule reads this as a genuine passing verdict for logic that was never actually exercised. The mechanical, non-name-shaped fix is to recognise argparse's own structural footprint (exit code 2 plus a 'usage: ' line) as a THIRD blocked cause, distinct from both the declared-input-missing cause and the run_hook.py not-run cause -- and to resolve the disabled/blocked-vs-unverified question by asking whether THIS runner's own subprocess launch already happened: unverified is reserved for a pre-execution declaration-level judgement (checked before any subprocess starts), blocked is for an attempt that was launched but could not reach a verdict, and a run_hook.py-mediated not-run report always falls in the second bucket because a real subprocess (run_hook.py itself) was genuinely started.

The H-1 rework's new _looks_like_argparse_usage_error() heuristic (exit code 2 + a 'usage: ' substring) is over-broad by construction: this repo already has a real, non-argparse precedent for exactly that shape. change_set_source.py's own main() prints a message containing 'usage: ' and returns exit code 2 for its own missing-argument / malformed-manifest convention (see change_set_source.py:331-341), completely independent of Python's argparse module. Any future check that shares this repo's own exit-2-plus-usage-line convention (not literal argparse) will be misclassified 'blocked' instead of 'passing' the day someone declares a negative_control for it -- a false-blocked, not a false-passing, so it cannot flip a gate's exit code (_sweep's any_failing only fires on STATE_FAILING), but it silently degrades the liveness record's accuracy for a check that is actually fine. General lesson for this whole family: a structural-footprint heuristic keyed on a generic marker (a bare exit code plus a common substring like 'usage: ') must be checked against every OTHER script in the same directory that might independently produce the same marker for an unrelated reason, not just against the one library (argparse) the heuristic was named after. The module's own docstring already hinted at the tighter, safer footprint ('usage: ... / error: unrecognized arguments') but the implemented check only requires the single weaker marker -- narrower verification than the documented intent.

check_done_proof.py's _composite_child_ids (BO-2500b-1-iii) treats ANY AC whose covered_by contains an AC-id-shaped entry (no path separator, no .py/.ts/.tsx suffix) as a composite that can only reach work_status: done once every one of those named children is itself done-and-covered -- and this applies regardless of the AC's own level field. GE-120f-1 is an L2 whose covered_by names two still-todo Roman-suffixed children (GE-120f-1-i, GE-120f-1-ii); even though this ticket's own diff genuinely and independently demonstrates GE-120f-1's own Gherkin clauses (9/9 tests green, mutation-proofed, ac-validator signed off clause-by-clause), setting work_status: done here would be refused by the pre-commit check_staged_done_proofs hook as an unproven-child violation -- the ACD-400a-shaped failure this whole tree exists to prevent, one level up. Lesson for future ac-fulfillment-gate runs: before flipping any AC's work_status to done, always check whether its own covered_by contains AC-id children (not just test-file paths) and, if so, check those children's own work_status first -- a generic diff-intersection check alone (files_touched present in the diff) is not sufficient evidence for a composite-shaped AC. covered_by can validly hold a MIX of AC-id children and real test-file paths on the same record (per BO-2500b-1-iii's own decision history); appending real covering test paths alongside existing AC-id children is safe and does not disturb the composite-child count, which is computed by excluding path-like entries via the regex [/\\]|\.(py|ts|tsx)$.

Deploy-phase globbing is a per-phase fact, not a directory fact. build_template_standalone_scripts globs templates/scripts/*.py FLAT by design, and scripts/build.py::_manifest_sync_platforms_scripts documents widening it to rglob as an already-rejected fix (KI-BP-023) because a manifest must mirror its PHASE, not its directory. So any new nested source under templates/scripts/<subdir>/ needs a NEW deploy phase plus its own mirroring _manifest_* helper, authored in the same change. When enriching any AC whose delivery is 'a script reaches a consumer install', verify which phase actually picks the path up before assuming any phase does.

The propagation audit resolves references in a layout-agnostic 'scripts/<rel>' key space, but a real build deploys scripts under the output root (observed .leafcutter/scripts/). A resolving guard key therefore does NOT prove the bare relative path an arrived agent/skill template instructs actually resolves from where a consumer's authors work. Two live instances measured 2026-09-14: write-c4-diagram SKILL.md's 'scripts/scaffold/new_arch_doc.py' and architecture-diagram-author.md's 'leafcutter/scripts/next_diagram_seq.py'. Templates must state invocation paths via the output-root placeholder; a green propagation audit is not evidence for that clause and the two concerns belong in separate ACs.

Enriching a 'remove a suppression from a guard' AC: the two-run movement (delivered->silent, withheld->reported) is necessary but not sufficient. Two extra it_requirements are load-bearing. (1) The last-clause evasion: relocating the entry from EXTERNAL_DEPENDENCY_ALLOWLIST to KNOWN_UNDEPLOYED_ALLOWLIST passes both runs while keeping the guard quiet, so require both allowlists be read directly. (2) The wrong-remedy failure: build_propagation_audit._suggest_action branches on a hardcoded _PREFIXES_WITH_EXISTING_DEPLOY_PHASE tuple, so a new deploy-phase prefix must be added there in the same change or the guard reports a truthful finding with an untruthful corrective action - visible only to a test that asserts the suggested_action, not merely that an entry was emitted.

Enriching any AC whose criteria say 'the produced artifact passes the project's own checks': do NOT let that clause be the observation. Measured 2026-09-14. (1) check_diagram_naming.py and check_mermaid_parent_link.py derive their input from `git diff --cached` and ignore argv entirely, returning 0 after inspecting zero files - so a harness that generates into a tmpdir and runs them without `git init` + `git add` gets a silent pass. Require the harness to stage the output AND pair every hook run with a negative control the hook must reject. check_doc_frontmatter.py does accept --file/--all and reports an inspected count; require the count be asserted non-zero. (2) A declared obligation can be policed by nothing: config/diagram_types.json declares per-genre requires_frontmatter (data_flow->related_code, user_flow->related_surfaces, agent_flow->related_agents) and the string `requires_frontmatter` appears in exactly one Python file in the repo, inside a docstring. diagram_type_validators.validate_diagram_type checks the genre NAME and stops. frontmatter_validators.validate_paths only path-checks related_docs/related_code/architecture_diagrams, so related_surfaces and related_agents are unobserved by every hook. Before writing an it_requirement of the form 'and the checks will catch X', grep for the field name across the enforcing surfaces - a declared-but-unenforced obligation means the AC's test must assert directly against the produced artifact.

Staging the file is NOT enough to defeat the vacuous-green trap in check_mermaid_parent_link.py - a second, independent mechanism survives it. Measured 2026-09-14. The hook sets REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2] as a MODULE-LEVEL constant derived from the hook file's own location, while _get_staged_files() reads the cwd repo's index. In a tmpdir scratch repo the two disagree, every abs_path.exists() is False, _check_arch_doc returns [] and the hook exits 0 having read neither the child nor the parent - even with a correct `git init` + `git add`. The fix is to place the scratch collection where the hook's __file__-relative root and the cwd-relative index resolve to the SAME directory (copy scripts/commit_guardian/ + config/ into the scratch repo at equal relative depth). A third silencer: _bypass_active() reads the LAST COMMIT's subject via `git log -1 --format=%s`, and check_diagram_naming reads .git/COMMIT_EDITMSG, so [NO-ARCH-UPDATE] anywhere in the harness's history no-ops them. Separately: when an AC enumerates 'the project's document checks', derive the set from the hooks manifest's per-hook `files:` regex, not from the AC's prose. docs/architecture/**.md matches SIX judgment-tier hooks, not the four typically named - check-description-field (^docs/.*\.md$, requires a non-empty description:) and check-surface-components-e2 are the two always forgotten, and SKILL.md's frontmatter checklist omits description: entirely while publishing a verification command (--files) the script's argparse does not accept.

Decomposing a documentation_triggers L1 into a documentation L2: the default criterion ('a how-to exists covering X') is satisfied by a stub, so bind the page to something runnable and assert a BIJECTION rather than a presence. Two shapes worked for INF-1300: (1) troubleshooting page <-> the implementation's own refusal-reason set, derived at run time from the shared refusal path, checked both ways (a reason with no entry AND an entry for a reason that cannot occur are both failures), plus an executed remedy arm - provoke the real refusal, apply exactly what the entry says, re-run, put the result through the real hooks; (2) reference page <-> a declaration (config/diagram_types.json), with movement arms - add a kind, retire a kind, change a kind's notation, each with nothing else altered, and the suite must redden. CLAUDE.md's 'Verify Behaviorally, Not by Grep' applies to markdown whenever the page's content is derivable from a declaration. Two further BA-level traps. GATE SET: config/guardrail_gates.yaml maps docs/{auth,privacy,safety,cost} to EMPTY agent lists, so those pairings compute zero gate agents; docs/contract_boundary is [documentation-expert, pr-reviewer], and change_target: [code, docs] + contract_boundary unions the real reviewers in - verify the pairing in the YAML before setting it. DUPLICATION FENCE: when a sibling AC already owns correcting a prose surface, the new doc AC must reference rather than restate it, and that fence belongs in the CRITERIA (artifact-against-artifact block comparison), not in a style note - otherwise the corrected content acquires a third copy the next correction will not reach.

KM-400 decomposition: documentation ACs were authored as L3 children of the behavioural L2 they document, not as L2 children of the L1. Reason: check_ac_limits caps an L1 at 5 L2 children (_MAX_L2_PER_L1) and KM-400's seven L1s carry eleven documentation_triggers between them, so the L2-doc-AC convention overflows the cap on any L1 with 3+ triggers plus 3 behaviours. The L3 placement also states the real dependency (a reference cannot be written before the behaviour it describes is fixed) and satisfies the documentation-AC rule that depends_on names the behavioural AC. Apply uniformly per tree, not case by case.

knowledge-management convention confirmed 2026-09-30: the KM-400 tree uses plain KM-NNN ids, so unlike KM-ADM-* / KM-KGS-* the derive_parent_id-based hooks DO fire. Verified all 41 new records: derived parent exists, parent id is in the child's depends_on, and the child id is in the parent's covered_by. The compound-prefix blind spot recorded in PROJECT_CONTEXT does not apply here and the back-links are load-bearing rather than conventional.

When a /plan-feature run has a product-truth mock-data artifact for the component (docs/product-truth/mock-data/<product>/<name>.mock.json), read it BEFORE authoring L2s even when index.json by_component lists no flow. The knowledge-api dataset supplied every concrete value the Gherkin needed - real revisions, version pairs, coverage figures, policy dispositions - and its `invariants` array is effectively a pre-written list of L2/L3 candidates. Decomposing from the L1 prose alone would have produced weaker, vaguer criteria.

declares_side_effect is derived and blocking, so phrase Then clauses deliberately: use 'a <noun> file is written to <dest>' ONLY where the AC genuinely persists something (and then set declares_side_effect: true), and avoid 'is written' entirely on documentation ACs, whose deliverable is a file but whose criteria should describe content. Verified the whole KM-400 folder against derive_declares_side_effect() before reporting - zero mismatches.

BA cross-check that paid off on KM-400: verify the relevance prose on an inherited doc_links entry actually matches the record it cites. KM-400a cited KM-KQS-034 with relevance text describing importlib file-path loading; KM-KQS-034 is about Agent Protocol graceful degradation, and the text describes KM-KQS-010. A doc_links entry that points at a real, existing file passes every hook while sending the implementing agent to the wrong record.

The BO-2000d package-surface validator keys on the SCALAR component being build_pipeline or build-orchestration, never on the components LIST. KM-400b-1 is scalar component knowledge-management with components [knowledge_management, build_pipeline] and assigned_agent python-coder, and it is correctly NOT package-surface, so plain-list it_requirements apply. Check the scalar before reaching for the five-key structured object; getting this wrong either files a fictional reference_file_path or blocks a genuine package-surface AC.

Enriching an API-contract tree: check the packaging prerequisite before accepting an 'importable module' AC as scoped. KM-400a-3 requires 'from leafcutter.knowledge import api' from an installed distribution, but this repo has NO pyproject.toml, setup.py or setup.cfg at the root and no leafcutter/ package - everything is under scripts/ and reached by path. The AC is not greenfield-with-a-helper, it carries an entire packaging step. Name that as an it_requirement rather than letting a coder discover it, and raise it as a caveat at the gate.

Recurring it_requirement shape for any 'works with X absent' AC: the absence must be ARRANGED, not assumed, and the isolation harness itself needs a discrimination test. A subprocess absence test passes on the author's machine whenever the checkout happens to be importable, so pair every project-absent assertion with a test that feeds the harness a path which DOES include the checkout and asserts it reports reachable. Applied to KM-400a-3 and KM-400b-2.

Default-deny export policy: the enforceable it_requirement is structural, not a check. Require the exporter to ITERATE THE POLICY and pull what it names, never to iterate discovered material and filter it - a filter fails open for anything it did not anticipate; an iteration over the policy cannot. Same family as the data-driven-exemption rule: exemption derives from absence of an approving entry, never from a hard-coded surface name. Applied to KM-400d-1; the 'never' disposition (KM-400d-3) needs the stronger form again, structurally unreachable rather than an ungranted opt-in.

A BA tree whose ACs repeatedly say 'X is its own state, never folded into Y' (KM-400b-3-i unknown, KM-400c-1-i whole-file reason, KM-400e-3 unversioned, KM-400f-2 built-but-unproved, KM-400g-3 staleness-vs-conflict) has one unnamed load-bearing technical constraint behind all of them: the classifying function must be TOTAL over its inputs with an explicit branch per state and no default arm. State it once per AC as the it_requirement, and pair it with a partition/sum invariant asserted by the implementation rather than only by tests - errors that cancel keep the totals adding up while the classification is wrong.

Documentation ACs placed at L3 (the KM-400 level deviation) do not change IT-PO enrichment: they still take assigned_agent documentation-expert or architecture-diagram-author, test_required false with a test_rationale, and it_requirements about frontmatter + docs/INDEX.md registration + a generated-or-mechanically-checked-against-the-implementation clause. The recurring one worth copying: require the reference to be derived from the implementation's own vocabulary in BOTH directions, so an operation/outcome/anchor-kind added later cannot leave the reference describing a subset while reading as complete.

ac-driven-dev decomposition pattern: when a defect contradicts an already-approved done L2 whose L1 is at the 5-child cap (_MAX_L2_PER_L1 = 5, _MAX_L1_PER_L0 = 7 in check_ac_limits.py), author the new behaviours as Roman-suffixed L3 children of that L2 rather than as new L2 siblings. L2 parents have no child cap (_MAX_CHILDREN only keys L0 and L1), so this is the only shape that fits without a child_limit_override or a tree split. Record the recommended criteria amendment to the approved parent verbatim in the L3's notes for the user to apply at the approval gate -- the BA must not edit an approved sibling. Second pattern from the same run: a 'prefer X over Y' selection rule needs a MIRROR record (same fixture, origin swapped, expected copy swapped), because one record alone is satisfied by a fixed preference in either direction -- that is exactly how the KI-ACD-004 fix produced KI-ACD-20260927. Third: when a resolution supplies both an executable location and a data location, splitting them needs its own record, or the fix for the executable silently relocates the data.

Three fast-lane L0s are now routinely confused and the distinction must be checked before authoring: BO-2400/2400f (the ARC — one id in, PR or refusal out), BO-3500 (the RANGE of work the arc can carry — producer routing AND non-code proof, deliberately one goal), BO-4200 (the TRUTH of the verdict — breadth, honesty of scope, consequence, cost, and misattributed refusals). A roster/producer-widening request is already covered end to end by BO-3500 down to L2 (BO-3500a names frontend, documentation and prompt work in its own tagline; BO-3500c owns the test_required/proof half); new measurements are grounds for raising that tree's priority (currently medium), not for a second tree. Structural rule learned: a Pattern C intermediate split of BO-2400f is NOT available, because Pattern C creates sibling L1s under the same L0 and BO-2400 is at 7 of 7 with an explicit fence against an eighth — the split discharges one cap by breaching the other, and additionally forces renaming L2s that are already work_status done with implemented_by populated. A sibling L0 (Pattern A) is the correct destination and is the second time this component has reached that conclusion against the same two fenced records.
